rules_evaluated.name: Referent resolution under sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Judgement. Session-artifact carve-out covers 'the ticket'/'the bug you fixed'/'a failing test' throughout (lines 13, 21, 30, 55, 60, 65, 69, 74 — all definite refs to the student's own session). Chunk 6's 'The loop that started with a failing test closed' (line 74) uses 'the loop', which is arc-earned spine vocabulary named in the enclosing module file getting-going.md Key Concepts ('The loop is orient -> fix -> close -> compound', line 57) before this exercise's include (line 48) — carve-out per rule 1's module-arc clause applies, no re-earning owed. Chunk 4's 'it' (line 65, 'Does it sound like...') is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject, not a violation. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referents found.

rules_evaluated.name: Cross-file and positional callbacks
rules_evaluated.evidence: Judgement. Only external pointer is line 53's named link to reference/mcp-and-connectors.md, named by title not located by position — satisfies the surviving requirement even though the open policy question in the compendium's §13 is moot for this file (no in-body positional link). No 'the opening lecture said' style cross-file callback found. Line 74's session-artifact/spine-vocab reference to fix-tests-first's beat is not a file pointer (uses 'the loop' + 'a failing test', both exempt session/arc vocabulary), so it does not trip §2.
